sentences: I check the rain gauge every morning at seven and write the measurement in my notebook.
I listen to the rain hitting the metal roof and count the seconds between thunderclaps.
I open my umbrella when the first drops fall and close it when the rain stops.
I watch the water flow down the street gutter and disappear into the storm drain.
I put on my raincoat and boots before stepping outside into the steady drizzle.
I check the weather app on my phone to see when the rain will start today.
I wipe the condensation off the window to look at the rain falling on the garden.
I empty the overflow bucket under the downspout and measure how much water it collected.
I walk around the puddles on the sidewalk to keep my shoes from getting wet.
I bring the laundry inside from the line when the first raindrops hit the dry clothes.
I note the time the rain begins and the time it ends on my daily log sheet.
I cover the outdoor grill with a plastic tarp before the heavy rain arrives tonight.
I step outside into the light misty rain and note the damp air on my face and hands.
I check the basement floor for water after several hours of continuous rainfall.
I use a squeegee to push the rainwater off the driveway and toward the street.
I take a photograph of the rain gauge to record the exact water level for my records.
I hear the rain tapping on the air conditioner unit outside my bedroom window.
I empty the small plastic container I set on the porch to catch the falling rain.
I check the soil moisture in the garden after a long night of steady rain.
I close the car windows and turn on the wipers when the rain starts on my drive home.
